subject: Literature
title: The Aeneid and the Founding Myth of Rome
description: A quick win: understand The Aeneid and the Founding Myth of Rome.

hook.text: Emperor Augustus wanted a national epic, so Virgil spent eleven years writing one and then begged to burn it.

buildup.text: The Aeneid follows the Trojan hero Aeneas as he journeys to Italy to found the civilization that becomes Rome.

discovery.text: Virgil modeled his epic on Homer but gave it a political mission: to justify Augustus's imperial rule.

twist.text: Virgil died before finishing it and ordered its destruction. Augustus overruled the dead poet and published it.

climax.text: The Aeneid showed how mythology can be weaponized as political propaganda to legitimize power.

punchline.text: A poet who wanted his work burned created Rome's identity.

quiz.question: What happened after Virgil died before finishing the Aeneid?
options: His students completed it in his style
Augustus overruled his wish and published it
It was lost for a thousand years
